item.title: Migrate Desk to React, Jotai, Wouter and Tailwind with Oxc tooling

body:
## Goal

Migrate Desk from Svelte to a client-rendered React SPA with Jotai, Wouter and Tailwind CSS. Improve maintainability and development tooling without regressing behavior, responsiveness or resource use. Accepted for implementation on November 8, 2026. Implement the migration described below as its own scope, separate from JOB-139. Begin with the screen/behavior inventory and measured Svelte baseline, set numeric acceptance budgets before porting, then continue through implementation, parity verification and removal of Svelte. Inventory and baseline are the first implementation slice, not a separate proposal requiring renewed approval. Preserve the acceptance, review and deployment gates below.

## Completion gate

JOB-150 is not complete until the actual React migration, parity/performance verification, Svelte removal and packaging/CI updates below are delivered. PR #1092 (b79e7eb) completed only the inventory/baseline prerequisite, not the migration. Continue from its recorded baseline and budgets. Do not close this issue after a prerequisite, documentation-only PR, app-shell-only PR or other partial slice. If multiple PRs are needed, keep this issue open and explicitly track and start the remaining implementation until every acceptance criterion is met. Partial work must not be reported as shipped migration. Review and post-merge acceptance must evaluate the entire issue, not just whether one PR merged and deployed.

## Agreed stack

* React + TypeScript + Vite. Keep static assets embedded and served by Go. No Waku, SSR service, Node production server or replacement backend.
* Jotai for live application data and transient UI state. Wouter for routes, route parameters and URL state. Do not mirror navigation state in atoms unnecessarily.
* Tailwind CSS is required, integrated into Vite. Preserve and unify existing semantic design tokens through shared theme/CSS variables for colors, spacing, typography, borders, focus and interaction states. Keep light/dark themes, compact density and lowercase controls. This is not an unrelated visual redesign.
* Base UI for accessible unstyled dialogs, menus, popovers and tooltips, styled with Tailwind and shared tokens. Reuse small app-level components rather than duplicating control styling across screens.
* React adapter for TanStack Virtual where long chats, journals or ticket lists need virtualization. Preserve scroll anchoring, variable-height content, selection, keyboard navigation and accessibility.
* Fuse.js for shared client-side fuzzy search in chat/ticket pickers and other local collections. Prioritize exact identifiers, define searchable fields and weights explicitly, reuse indexes where practical, and keep indexes synchronized with live additions, updates and removals. Server-side/global searches remain authoritative. Do not imply a partial loaded collection is the complete searchable dataset.
* `@tanstack/react-hotkeys` for shared scoped keyboard shortcuts, not `react-hotkeys-hook`. Pin supported versions and check release maturity during implementation. Scope shortcuts to the active screen or overlay, avoid firing during text entry or IME composition, preserve browser/OS shortcuts and let Base UI own dialog focus/Escape behavior. Provide platform-appropriate shortcut labels without duplicate registrations across route changes.
* Oxlint and Oxfmt for lint/format, alongside explicit TypeScript type checking. Use the Oxc-backed Vite React transform and Oxc React Compiler integration after checking supported versions and compatibility. Record any experimental limitations and fallback, rather than assuming compiler integration is stable or required for correctness.
* Preserve the existing Markdown renderer/sanitizer and qualified GitHub reference behavior. Use the React icon package equivalent of the current icon set.
* Retain Playwright acceptance tests and the generated Go client/transport. Use browser-native fetch, SSE, uploads, clipboard and Intl where sufficient.

## State and transport architecture

Keep Go → existing API/SSE → shared Jotai store → routed React screens.

Place a stable Jotai Provider/store and connection ownership above routed screens. Navigation must not recreate the store, reopen the connection unnecessarily or drop live updates. Components rendered by Wouter read/write atoms normally, without a custom router-state bridge.

Use stable per-ticket/session identities and narrow subscriptions. Separate list membership/order from individual entity contents, preserve unchanged references and avoid a giant snapshot atom consumed by every component. Handle initial snapshots, patches, reconnects, removals and stale selections consistently. Ensure logout/endpoint changes clear scoped data and do not mix controllers' state.

Preserve proxy-prefix routing, deep links, browser back/forward, refresh behavior, CSRF/auth, cancellation, error handling and current no-polling live behavior. Choose hash/path routing based on existing Go serving requirements, not by introducing a new server.

## Dependency boundaries

Do not add a separate query cache alongside Jotai, a form library, date library, full data grid or broad UI framework without a concrete requirement. Native HTML controls remain appropriate for simple inputs. Inventory graph requirements before choosing an additional package: retain the current renderer if it meets temporal layout, pan/zoom, selection and keyboard needs. Avoid introducing React Flow or a layout engine merely because the framework changed.

## Migration plan

1. Inventory every existing screen, route, overlay, transport boundary and acceptance scenario. Map behavior and tests before editing, including home, trace/graph/history, learn, sys/audit, catch-up, chat and mobile navigation.
2. Measure the current Svelte production build and development toolchain on representative real data. Record test environment, dataset and reproducible commands. Set numeric acceptance budgets before the port, not after observing results.
3. Build the React app shell, Tailwind token mapping, shared accessible primitives, routing/store boundary and one representative live screen. Keep the existing application runnable while validating the candidate, without duplicate action submissions or connections.
4. Compare the candidate with the baseline before expanding. React Compiler and Oxc are tools, not proof of better performance. Do not claim transform-vs-Babel benchmarks establish faster compilation than Svelte.
5. Port screens with behavior parity, retaining existing Go API/SSE contracts. Reuse Markdown, transport and other framework-independent code. Preserve URL compatibility or provide explicit redirects.
6. Remove Svelte, its plugin/checker, obsolete components, duplicated CSS and unused dependencies only after full parity and performance verification. Update scripts, lockfile, embedded assets, Nix/CI integration and contributor documentation together.

## Required parity

* Desktop/mobile layout, compact sizing, token-based themes, hover/focus/cursor states and lowercase controls.
* Chat creation, switching, drafts, Markdown, native image/document attachments, uploads/paste, streaming and reload restoration.
* Ticket titles and hover identifiers, leading status indicators, filters, links, trace selection, meaningful history and step names.
* Graph temporality, hand panning, zoom and existing visibility toggles.
* Live system and automation audit: ordered event/invocation/attempt/call evidence, UNKNOWN states, redacted data, bounded artifacts and resulting-ticket links.
* Loading/empty/error/disconnected states, accessible names, focus restoration, keyboard navigation and reduced-motion handling where applicable.

## Acceptance

* Production build, TypeScript check, Oxlint, Oxfmt and applicable Go/UI/Nix CI pass. Generated embedded assets are current and the packaged Go binary serves the SPA without an extra runtime service.
* Existing acceptance tests are ported rather than weakened. Real desktop/mobile browser workflows exercise the actual Go controller and API/SSE, including reconnects, navigation, attachments, audit and graph interaction. Add focused regressions only for uncovered application behavior, not dependency behavior or disposable scaffolding.
* Compare cold/warm production build, dev startup/HMR, compressed JS/CSS, first usable render, browser heap/CPU, sustained SSE bursts, large-list scrolling and interaction latency against the recorded Svelte baseline. Require no material regression against agreed budgets, and document results and tradeoffs. Equal runtime performance is a target, not an unmeasured claim.
* Verify no duplicate SSE connections, polling regressions, action duplication, cross-endpoint state leakage, sanitizer regressions or route-refresh failures.
* Verify Fuse search against real local data: exact-ID priority, weighted matching, empty/no-result states, live index updates/removals and bounded latency on representative large collections. Verify shortcuts across routes/overlays, text inputs, contenteditable fields, IME composition, modifier/platform differences and keyboard layouts. Test application behavior rather than library internals.
* Document package ownership, state/route conventions, Tailwind tokens/components, development commands, performance reproduction, migration and rollback. Keep implementation scoped to the frontend migration unless an independently justified backend fix is necessary.

This is the full React migration: Svelte removed, budgets measured and met, e2e 65 passed on desktop and mobile and behind a path prefix, nix and CI updated, rollback documented in docs/notes/JOB-150-desk-react-port.md. The issue stays open until review checks the whole acceptance list. Code change.

comments.author: elee-agent
comments.body: Not work (no PR opened). The description says this is a backlog proposal, not authorization to start implementation, and the approved target JOB-139 explicitly left it out (Desk React migration, too large to mix in). Its own plan also requires a screen inventory and numeric performance budgets on the Svelte baseline before any port, which need a human decision. Moving it back to Backlog so intake does not restart it. To start it, a human should approve it as its own target and say whether step 1 to 2 (inventory and baseline) is the first slice.
